rubrics.rubric: Does the Compliance Matrix accurately represent every employee-course compliance state using the instructed five statuses and an auditable as-of date?
criterion: The matrix covers all 45 employees and every course identified as OSHA-required from the source records and OSHA reference.
Each employee-course entry uses exactly Current, Expiring within 60 days, Overdue, Never Completed, or Failed.
Each entry includes the date of last completion or N/A when the course was never completed.
Expiring within 60 days is calculated from Refresher_Due_Date relative to a stated early-2025 as-of date.
The sheet documents how Completed, Incomplete, Failed, Overdue, and no-record source states map to the five displayed statuses.
When multiple attempts exist, the selected status and last-completion date follow a stated, consistently applied rule.

rubrics.rubric: Are the composite employee-risk ranking and Department Risk Dashboard calculated transparently from the supplied compliance, incident, recency, and survey data?
criterion: The composite risk formula is documented on the workbook and includes compliance failures, departmental incident exposure, and recency for incident-correlated courses.
The formula is applied consistently to all employees without manually forcing expected names or departments into the ranking.
The 10 employees with the highest calculated scores are visibly highlighted and each has a note explaining the score components.

The dashboard contains all eight departments with compliance percentage, overdue OSHA item count, training-related incident count, average survey satisfaction, risk-priority rank, and explanatory notes.
Department counts and rankings reconcile to the employee matrix, incident log, and survey data.

rubrics.rubric: Does the 13-week Q2 training plan satisfy the date, resource, participant, cost, and budget constraints in executable session rows?
criterion: The schedule covers April 7 through July 4, 2025 and provides week, date, course code and name, format, room, instructor, participants, and session cost for every session.
Each session respects the instructor availability, specialization, room availability, facility suitability, and session limits in Resource Availability.
In-person sessions cost 650 dollars plus 200 dollars per instructor and virtual sessions cost 250 dollars plus 200 dollars per instructor.
A running weekly and cumulative cost tally is shown and remains at or below the 38,000 dollar cap.
Participants or an attached roster make it possible to verify which overdue or failed employee-course requirements each remediation session covers.
Course prioritization reconciles incident root-cause evidence and survey evidence with a documented explanation when those signals conflict.

rubrics.rubric: Does the schedule provide timely compliance remediation and monthly coverage for every incident-linked OSHA course?
criterion: Every employee with an overdue or failed OSHA-required course is assigned to a suitable remediation session within the first four weeks.
Every OSHA-required course with at least one Training_Related = Yes incident has at least one scheduled session in April, May, and June.
Monthly coverage is verifiable from dated session rows rather than asserted only in narrative text.
The schedule does not substitute a non-OSHA course for an incident-linked OSHA course merely to satisfy the coverage count.

rubrics.rubric: Do Sections 1 and 2 of the Integrated Evaluation Framework diagnose reaction-outcome disconnects and redesign the Level 1 survey from the actual evidence?
criterion: The PDF is 6 to 10 pages and begins with three courses whose Level 1 satisfaction most meaningfully diverges from their safety outcomes, using the supplied survey and incident data.
The retrospective analysis explains what those disconnects reveal about relying on reaction scores as safety evidence.
The redesigned survey contains items tied to observed weaknesses in the current ratings, delivery formats, and recurring open-feedback themes.
The survey includes a retrospective before-and-after knowledge matrix on a 5-point scale consistent with the NC State Tool-1A approach.
The redesigned items are usable as an instrument rather than only described as recommendations.

rubrics.rubric: Does Section 3 provide complete Levels 2-4 measures for the two courses selected by a documented, source-grounded course-risk method?
criterion: The two target courses are selected using a documented composite course-risk method based on relevant compliance, incident, severity, recency, or outcome evidence; no hidden expected course identities are required.
Each target course has an 8 to 10 item pre/post knowledge assessment testing specific regulatory or procedural knowledge.
Each knowledge item cites the applicable 29 CFR standard or subsection and has a verifiable correct answer or scoring key.
Each target course has a 90-day supervisor checklist of specific observable behaviors tied to applicable OSHA subsections.
Three KPIs state actual baselines from the supplied data and measurable end-of-Q3 2025 targets.
The measures distinguish Kirkpatrick learning, behavior, and results evidence.

rubrics.rubric: Does Section 4 present a transparent ROI projection using the actual incident baseline, a cited cost benchmark, and the plan's real investment?
criterion: The baseline explicitly states the incident-log observation period, including its start and end dates or an equivalent unambiguous range, together with 52 incidents, 23 OSHA recordables, and 129 lost work days.
The calculation cites an identifiable industry benchmark for OSHA-recordable incident cost and explains any lost-work-day cost treatment without double-counting.
The expected incident-reduction percentage and its rationale are stated.
Projected avoided cost, training cost, net benefit, and ROI are arithmetically consistent.
Training cost uses the actual scheduled plan cost and explicitly relates it to the 38,000 dollar cap; a full-cap scenario is acceptable when clearly labeled as a conservative alternative.
End-of-Q3 2025 targets are tied back to the stated baseline metrics.
